close_reason: Removed #[doc(hidden)] from CompositeVerifier::new, validate_attribute_cert, and verify_scts. Each function already has a # Limitations rustdoc block warning of stub status, which is the visible-but-loud signal the bead recommended.
description:
## Anchor
Pass-2 commit e586bc49 closed PKIX-qwzx.20 ("misuse of #[deprecated] on stub APIs in pkix-ac/pkix-ct/pkix-composite"). The fix replaced `#[deprecated]` with `#[doc(hidden)]` on:
- pkix_ac::validate_attribute_cert
- pkix_composite::CompositeVerifier::new
- pkix_ct::verify_scts

## Finding
The replacement `#[doc(hidden)]` has stronger consequences than `#[deprecated]`:
1. It removes the function from rustdoc output entirely (the function is not listed in the crate's documented surface).
2. It does NOT prevent compilation at call sites (verified: `cargo check` against `pkix_composite::CompositeVerifier::new(0u8, 0u8)` from an external crate succeeds with no warning).
3. There is no compiler signal at the call site that this is a stub.

The most problematic case is **pkix-composite/src/lib.rs:71-77**:
- `pub struct CompositeVerifier` is documented and rendered in rustdoc.
- `pub fn new` is the *only* constructor.
- `#[doc(hidden)]` on `new` means rustdoc users see the struct exists but have no documented way to construct one.

For pkix_ac::validate_attribute_cert and pkix_ct::verify_scts the same problem exists — the entry point is hidden, but the crate-level docs still describe the planned behavior.

## Severity
P3 / opinion. None of these stubs are functional yet, so users calling them just get `Err(...)`. But:
- Doc/API surface mismatch is exactly the kind of consistency issue PKIX-qwzx.20 was filed to address (it just shifted the inconsistency rather than fixing it).
- A user who reads the docs cannot discover the constructor.

## Fix options
- (preferred) Drop `#[doc(hidden)]` and instead add a prominent rustdoc `# Limitations` block (which is already there for two of the three) — let the function be visible and the docs make the stub status loud.
- Alternatively, restore `#[deprecated(note = "stub; not yet implemented")]` if the goal is a compile-time warning at call sites — that's the original PKIX-qwzx.20 motivation reversed but at least is consistent and visible.

## Pass-2 attribution
PKIX-qwzx.20 closure swapped one inconsistency for another.
title: P3: #[doc(hidden)] on pkix-composite::CompositeVerifier::new makes the only constructor invisible to users
